contentHtml:
Bringing your child to the UAE requires sponsoring them for a residence visa. At the start, the process seems overwhelming. However, it’s simpler than it sounds if you know the steps. A new resident or already settled in, this guide is for everyone. We’ll help you navigate the residence visa for child in UAE with process.

By the end of this post, you’ll:

  • Understand the steps
  • The documents needed, and
  • The costs involved. Let’s get started!

What is a UAE Residence Visa for a Child?

A UAE residence allows them to live in the country legally. A residence visa is a gateway to essential services like schooling and healthcare. The visa is valid for one, two, or three years. However, it depends on the visa type and where it’s issued.

The good news is that a renewal option is available. You can renew the visa when it expires. Therefore, your child can stay legally as long as you’re in the UAE.

Who Can Sponsor Their Child’s Residence Visa in the UAE?

To sponsor a child’s residence visa, there are a few basic rules. Here’s who qualifies to be a sponsor:

  • Parents: Both mothers and fathers can sponsor their children. In some cases, if the mother is the primary sponsor, extra documents might be required.
  • Valid Residency: The sponsor must have a valid UAE residency visa.
  • Minimum Income: The sponsor needs to earn a certain amount. Usually, it’s around AED 4,000 per month (or AED 3,000 with accommodation from the employer).
  • Job Status: The sponsor should be employed full-time or self-employed. Freelancers and business owners may need to show more financial proof.
  • Accommodation: You must provide proof of a stable home for your child. A tenancy contract (Ejari) in your name is usually required.

Special Cases for Mothers

  • If the mother is sponsoring, she might need a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the father.
  • In cases of divorce or separation, proof of sole custody is needed.

Important Requirements for Your Child’s Residence Visa

Must understand the visa requirements before applying:

  • Age: The child must be under 18. They can remain under sponsorship if they are studying. Allowed to live until they complete their higher education.
  • Health Insurance: All children must have health insurance that meets the UAE’s standards.
  • Accommodation: You need to show that your home meets family living standards. A tenancy contract (Ejari) will help.

Essential Documents You’ll Need

To avoid delays, gather these documents required for a UAE residence visa for a child before you apply:

Document What You Need
Child’s Passport Copy of the passport with at least six months’ validity.
Passport Photos Recent passport-sized photos (white background).
Sponsor’s Documents A copy of the sponsor’s passport and Emirates ID.
Birth Certificate Attested by authorities and translated if needed.
Proof of Accommodation Tenancy contract (Ejari) in the sponsor’s name.
Salary Certificate or Labor Contract To prove the minimum income requirement.
Health Insurance A valid policy for the child.

Step-by-Step Process to Apply for Your Child’s Residence Visa

B: Breaking down the steps to make the process easier. Know what is required to apply for a UAE residence visa for a child:

  1. Collect Documents: You should have all the necessary papers. Double-check that everything is correct and updated.
  2. Entry Permit (if your child is outside the UAE): Apply for an entry permit if your child is not already in the UAE. This is the first step before applying for a residence visa.
  3. Medical Fitness Test: If your child is above 18 (for higher education purposes), they may need a medical fitness test. Children under 18 usually do not need this.
  4. Submit the Application: Once the entry permit is approved, apply for the residence visa.
  5. Pay the Fees: At this stage, visa processing, Emirates ID issuance, and medical test fees are required.
  6. Receive the Visa: The visa will be stamped in your child’s passport after approval. Congratulations, your child is now a legal UAE resident UAE!

How to apply residence visa for a child in UAE is simplified in this blog part. Now, move on to it’s cost involved and other details.

Costs for Sponsoring a Child’s Residence Visa

The costs involved in sponsoring a child’s visa can vary, but here’s a general idea of the fees you can expect:

Service Cost Range (AED)
Entry Permit 500-600
Visa Stamping 500-800
Emirates ID 100-300
Health Insurance 700+ (per year)
Medical Tests (if required) 300-500
Typing Center Fees 100-200
Urgent Processing 200-500

Example Total Cost for Standard Application:

  • AED 2,000-3,000 for mainland UAE.
  • Slight variations in free zones.

Renewing Your Child’s Resident Visa

Residence visa renewal in Dubai has become easier than before. Don’t forget to renew the visa when it expires! It is advisable to save the reminder so that you can renew it before expiration. To renew, you’ll need documents such as an updated passport and Emirates ID. Along with, accommodation proof and renewed health insurance. It is wise to apply at the earliest time, at least 30 days before the visa expires. The renewal costs are similar to the initial application.

Special Considerations to Keep in Mind

Some cases require extra attention. As a sponsor, you need to consider these points:

  • Adopted Children: Provide adoption papers if you’ve adopted a child.
  • Children from a Previous Marriage: Show legal custody documents if the child is from a previous marriage.
  • Children with Special Needs: The UAE may offer exemptions. Sometimes, faster process for children with disabilities.

Common Challenges and How to Avoid Them

It’s not uncommon to face some bumps along the way. To tackle them is a real trick; here’s what you need to do:

  • Missing Documents: Make sure you double-check everything before submitting.
  • Issues with Accommodation: Ensure your tenancy contract is up to date and meets the standards.
  • Processing Delays: If you’re facing delays, consider professional assistance to speed up the process.
